hook.en: Bacteria defend themselves against viruses by chopping the viral DNA at exact sequences. We borrowed those scissors to cut any DNA where we want.
hook.kn: ಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾಗಳು ವೈರಸ್ DNA ಯನ್ನು ನಿಖರ ಅನುಕ್ರಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಕತ್ತರಿಸಿ ತಮ್ಮನ್ನು ರಕ್ಷಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತವೆ. ಆ ಕತ್ತರಿಗಳನ್ನು ನಾವು ಎರವಲು ಪಡೆದು ಬೇಕಾದಲ್ಲಿ DNA ಕತ್ತರಿಸುತ್ತೇವೆ.

objectives.en: Explain how restriction endonucleases are named and how they recognise palindromes
Explain sticky ends and the role of DNA ligase
Describe separation of DNA fragments by agarose gel electrophoresis

narration.en: Bacteria defend themselves against viruses by chopping the viral DNA at exact sequences. We borrowed those scissors to cut any DNA where we want.
narration.kn: ಬ್ಯಾಕ್ಟೀರಿಯಾಗಳು ವೈರಸ್ DNA ಯನ್ನು ನಿಖರ ಅನುಕ್ರಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಕತ್ತರಿಸಿ ತಮ್ಮನ್ನು ರಕ್ಷಿಸಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತವೆ. ಆ ಕತ್ತರಿಗಳನ್ನು ನಾವು ಎರವಲು ಪಡೆದು ಬೇಕಾದಲ್ಲಿ DNA ಕತ್ತರಿಸುತ್ತೇವೆ.

body.en: In 1963 two enzymes that restrict the growth of bacteriophage were isolated from E. coli: one adds methyl groups to DNA, the other cuts DNA (restriction endonuclease). The first restriction endonuclease, Hind II, always cut DNA at a particular point by recognising a specific sequence of six base pairs, its recognition sequence. Today more than 900 restriction enzymes are known from over 230 strains of bacteria. Naming: in EcoRI, E = genus Escherichia, co = species coli, R = strain RY13, I = the first enzyme isolated from that strain. Nucleases are of two kinds: exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends of DNA, while endonucleases cut at specific positions within it.

points.en: Hind II: first restriction endonuclease, 6-bp recognition sequence
EcoRI: E-co (Escherichia coli), R (strain RY13), I (first isolated)
Exonuclease: cuts from ends; endonuclease: cuts within

narration.en: Restriction endonucleases cut DNA inside the molecule at specific recognition sequences. In the name EcoRI, E and co come from Escherichia coli, R is the strain RY13, and the Roman one shows it was the first enzyme isolated from that strain.
narration.kn: ನಿರ್ಬಂಧಕ ಎಂಡೋನ್ಯೂಕ್ಲಿಯೇಸ್‌ಗಳು DNA ಯನ್ನು ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಗುರುತಿನ ಅನುಕ್ರಮದಲ್ಲಿ ಒಳಗೆ ಕತ್ತರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. EcoRI ಹೆಸರಿನಲ್ಲಿ E ಮತ್ತು co ಎಶರೀಕಿಯಾ ಕೋಲೈ, R ಎಂದರೆ RY13 ತಳಿ, I ಎಂದರೆ ಆ ತಳಿಯಿಂದ ಮೊದಲು ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕಿಸಿದ ಕಿಣ್ವ.

say.en: EcoRI recognises the six-base sequence GAATTC. Read five prime to three prime, both strands say the same thing: it is a palindrome.
EcoRI cuts each strand between G and A, a little away from the centre, so the two pieces are left with single-stranded overhangs.
These overhangs are sticky ends. Cut the vector and the gene with the same enzyme and their ends pair up; DNA ligase then seals them.
To sort the fragments we use agarose gel electrophoresis. DNA is negative, so it moves towards the anode, and smaller fragments move farther through the gel.

narration.en: EcoRI recognises the six-base sequence GAATTC. Read five prime to three prime, both strands say the same thing: it is a palindrome. EcoRI cuts each strand between G and A, a little away from the centre, so the two pieces are left with single-stranded overhangs. These overhangs are sticky ends. Cut the vector and the gene with the same enzyme and their ends pair up; DNA ligase then seals them. To sort the fragments we use agarose gel electrophoresis. DNA is negative, so it moves towards the anode, and smaller fragments move farther through the gel.

body.en: Each restriction endonuclease recognises a palindromic nucleotide sequence: the sequence reads the same on the two strands when both are read in the same direction (5′→3′). For EcoRI it is 5′-GAATTC-3′ on one strand and 5′-GAATTC-3′ on the other (3′-CTTAAG-5′ read below). EcoRI cuts each strand between G and A, a little away from the centre of the palindrome, leaving single-stranded overhangs called sticky ends. Sticky ends form hydrogen bonds with complementary cut ends, so if a vector and the source DNA are cut with the same enzyme, their ends match; DNA ligase then seals them to give recombinant DNA.

points.en: Cut between G and A → sticky ends (overhangs)
Same enzyme for vector and insert → matching ends

narration.en: Restriction enzymes recognise palindromes such as GAATTC and cut a little off-centre, leaving sticky single-stranded ends. Cutting vector and gene with the same enzyme gives matching ends that DNA ligase joins.
narration.kn: ನಿರ್ಬಂಧಕ ಕಿಣ್ವಗಳು GAATTC ಯಂತಹ ಪ್ಯಾಲಿಂಡ್ರೋಮ್ ಗುರುತಿಸಿ ಕೇಂದ್ರದಿಂದ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪ ದೂರದಲ್ಲಿ ಕತ್ತರಿಸಿ ಅಂಟುವ ತುದಿಗಳನ್ನು ಬಿಡುತ್ತವೆ. ವಾಹಕ ಮತ್ತು ಜೀನನ್ನು ಒಂದೇ ಕಿಣ್ವದಿಂದ ಕತ್ತರಿಸಿದರೆ ಹೊಂದುವ ತುದಿಗಳು ಸಿಗುತ್ತವೆ; DNA ಲೈಗೇಸ್ ಅವನ್ನು ಜೋಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

body.en: Fragments produced by restriction enzymes are separated by gel electrophoresis. DNA is negatively charged, so in an electric field it moves towards the anode (positive electrode) through a matrix; the most common matrix is agarose, a natural polymer extracted from sea weeds. The gel acts as a sieve, so fragments separate by size: the smaller the fragment, the farther it moves. The separated DNA is seen only after staining with ethidium bromide and exposing to UV light, when it appears as bright orange bands. The bands are cut out and the DNA extracted from the gel piece; this is called elution.

points.en: DNA is negative → moves to the anode
Agarose (from sea weeds) acts as a sieve
Ethidium bromide + UV → orange bands; elution recovers DNA

narration.en: In gel electrophoresis, negatively charged DNA moves through agarose towards the anode, and smaller pieces travel farther. Ethidium bromide makes the bands glow orange under UV, and the wanted band is cut out and eluted.
narration.kn: ಜೆಲ್ ಎಲೆಕ್ಟ್ರೋಫೊರೆಸಿಸ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ಋಣಾವೇಶದ DNA ಅಗರೋಸ್ ಮೂಲಕ ಆನೋಡ್ ಕಡೆಗೆ ಚಲಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಸಣ್ಣ ತುಣುಕುಗಳು ಹೆಚ್ಚು ದೂರ ಹೋಗುತ್ತವೆ. ಎಥಿಡಿಯಂ ಬ್ರೋಮೈಡ್ UV ಬೆಳಕಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಕಿತ್ತಳೆ ಪಟ್ಟಿಗಳನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ; ಬೇಕಾದ ಪಟ್ಟಿಯನ್ನು ಕತ್ತರಿಸಿ ಹೊರತೆಗೆಯುತ್ತಾರೆ (ಇಲ್ಯೂಷನ್).

aim.en: To separate DNA fragments by agarose gel electrophoresis and estimate their sizes from a standard ladder.

narration.en: Load the DNA samples and switch on the current. Watch the fragments move towards the positive electrode and compare each band with the ladder to estimate its size.

caption.en: If the four bases occur at random, a particular n-base recognition sequence turns up about once in every 4^n base pairs. Longer sites mean fewer cuts and bigger fragments.

tryThis.en: EcoRI reads 6 bases: how often does it cut on average?
Switch from a 4-base cutter to an 8-base cutter. How do the fragment sizes change?
Which cutter would you choose to cut a 50 kb DNA into only a few pieces?

problem.en: A linear DNA molecule has three EcoRI sites. How many fragments are produced when it is cut completely with EcoRI, and in which direction do they move in an agarose gel?

steps.en: Each cut in a linear molecule adds one more piece: n cuts give n + 1 fragments.
DNA is negatively charged, so all fragments move towards the anode; the smallest moves farthest.

answer.en: 4 fragments, moving towards the anode (positive electrode), the smallest moving farthest.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. A linear DNA molecule has three EcoRI sites. How many fragments are produced when it is cut completely with EcoRI, and in which direction do they move in an agarose gel?

steps.en: Read the complementary strand from its 5′ end: 5′-GAATTC-3′.
Both strands read the same in the 5′→3′ direction.

answer.en: Both strands read GAATTC from 5′ to 3′, so it is a palindrome.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Show that 5′-GAATTC-3′ is a palindrome.
